title: Criminal Miscellaneous Petition under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for Quashing of FIR / Proceedings
whenToUse: Use when invoking inherent powers of High Court under Section 528 BNSS, 2023 to quash an FIR, chargesheet, or criminal complaint where allegations disclose a purely civil dispute or manifest abuse of law.
variantComparisonNote: Inherent jurisdiction petition before High Court under Section 528 BNSS. Replaces erstwhile Section 482 CrPC petitions.
youWillNeed: Certified copy of FIR, chargesheet / summoning order, commercial agreements establishing civil nature, correspondence proving compromise or mala fides.
legalBasis: Section 528 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS); State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (1992); Gian Singh v. State of Punjab (2012).
mandatoryStatutoryIngredients: Allegations even if taken at face value do not disclose any cognizable offense
Dispute is predominantly of a civil or commercial flavor
Proceeding manifestly instituted with mala fide or oblique intention
Interim stay on trial court coercive proceedings justified

particulars.label: Seat of High Court
particulars.description: Principal Bench or Circuit Bench city

particulars.label: Filing Date
particulars.description: Date of presentation before High Court

aiBlocks.title: Procedural History & Impugned FIR
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Set out procedural genesis, registration of impugned FIR No. {{FACT:fir_case_number}}, and nature of baseless criminal proceedings instituted by Respondent No. 2.

aiBlocks.title: Substantive Grounds under Bhajan Lal Principles
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Apply Bhajan Lal benchmarks demonstrating absence of ingredients of penal offenses under BNS, 2023, commercial transaction cloaked as crime, and abuse of process.

aiBlocks.title: Prayer for Quashing & Interim Relief
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Draft exhaustive prayer for quashing FIR No. {{FACT:fir_case_number}} and all consequential proceedings, with prayer for interim stay on coercive steps.
